name: PG&E Corporation
base_source: TTM non-GAAP core EPS: FY2025 $1.50 - H1 2025 $0.64 + H1 2026 $0.83 = $1.69; cross-checked TTM GAAP EPS $1.44 ($1.23 - $0.51 + $0.72). Engine base rejected: conservative OE (OCF - total capex) is negative all 5 FYs and TTM (OCF $8,147M = $8,716M - $3,905M + $3,336M, minus capex $12,410M = $11,787M - $5,700M + $6,323M = -$4,263M) - structural for a rate-base-growing utility mid-undergrounding program, not earning power. See analysis.md.
moat_justification: Legal-monopoly CA franchise with guided ~9-10% rate-base CAGR, >=9% core EPS growth through 2030, no new equity needed, and scarce Diablo Canyon nuclear - against CPUC-capped allowed ROE, inverse-condemnation wildfire liability that already bankrupted the equity once (2019-20), an original Wildfire Fund expected to be consumed by the Eaton fire with SB 254's $18B Continuation Account unfunded until 2029, AB 2700 restitution (~$6B unpaid FVT losses; dividends/equity named as mechanisms), and $57.5B net debt funding the growth.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 15.4x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Regulated California monopoly, moat 5/10 - on TTM core earnings of $1.69/share the $13.33 price (7.9x, half the peer multiple) yields an 18.2% weighted IRR with IV@15% of $16.98, clearing the 15% hurdle with the margin-of-safety price (~$14) right at today's quote; the discount is wildfire-tail compensation, not an operational discount.
